subject.title: feat(memory): add excludePaths option to memorySearch config

question: Should OpenClaw ship a builtin-only public `memorySearch.excludePaths` config key now, or should exclusion scope wait for the broader memory/QMD/recall eligibility design?
rationale: The mechanical blockers are repairable, but the PR adds a public config surface and explicitly leaves QMD unwired, so the permanent product boundary needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Ship builtin-only after repairs
options.body: Repair merge semantics, index identity, and docs generation, then ship the narrow builtin backend feature with the documented QMD caveat.

options.title: Require QMD parity first
options.body: Hold this PR until the same exclusion semantics are designed and tested for QMD indexing too.

options.title: Fold into broader path-scope design
options.body: Pause or supersede this PR in favor of the broader recall/index eligibility work tracked in the related feature issue.

recommendation.title: Ship builtin-only after repairs
recommendation.body: Repair merge semantics, index identity, and docs generation, then ship the narrow builtin backend feature with the documented QMD caveat.

likelyOwner.reason: This crosses memory indexing, public config, and published docs, where steipete has the strongest recent ownership trail among the related files.
